title: Data Types
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Data Types in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Integer (int)
items.text: int stores whole numbers without a decimal part.

items.heading: Float (float)
items.text: float stores numbers that have a decimal part.

items.heading: String (str)
items.text: str stores text written inside quotes.

items.heading: Boolean (bool)
items.text: bool represents a logical value: True or False.

items.heading: List
items.text: A list is an ordered, changeable collection. It is written with square brackets.

items.heading: Tuple
items.text: A tuple is an ordered collection that cannot normally be changed after creation. It uses parentheses.

items.heading: Set
items.text: A set is a collection of unique elements. Duplicate values are removed.

items.heading: Dictionary
items.text: A dictionary stores data as key-value pairs. It is written using braces with keys and values.

items.heading: None
items.text: None represents the absence of a value. It is commonly used when a value is not available or a function returns nothing explicitly.

items.heading: Checking a type
items.text: type() returns the type of a value or object.
